newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania envoy drops trip after talks with Berisha.
newsitem.headline: Albania envoy drops trip after talks with Berisha.

text.p: International mediator Franz Vranitzky on Wednesday unexpectedly cancelled a trip to the rebel-held south of chaotic Albania in an apparent gesture of goodwill to President Sali Berisha.

Vranitzky, an envoy for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), announced his decision not to travel to the trouble-hit port of Vlore on Thursday morning after holding more than an hour of talks with Berisha.
The president used the meeting to hammer home his message that the rebel committees controlling most of southern Albania were hindering progress towards the planned election in June.
Nearly 300 people have been killed and 700 wounded during weeks of armed anarchy that followed the collapse of fraudulent savings schemes.
Vranitzky, sharply criticised by pro-Berisha newspapers for having held contacts with the rebels last month, said the deadlock meant that the elections were "in a way imperilled".
After the meeting, OSCE spokeswoman Melissa Fleming said Vranitzky was dropping his plans to visit Vlore and Shkoder, a northern town which has been hit by fresh violence recently.
"He wants to focus on the situation here and on preparing for elections," she told reporters in Tirana.
Earlier on Wednesday, Vranitzky had said he would not let criticism of his contact with the rebels prevent him from carrying out his duties.
He said it had been useful to listen to rebel leaders but stressed he would only deal with the Albanian government.
Berisha said the committees were created by Prime Minister Bashkim Fino's Socialist Party, which was in opposition until joining a unity government with his Democratic Party in March.
"The committees are a Socialist Party creation," Berisha told Vranitzky at the meeting, attended by reporters.
Asked by Vranitzky whether the problem could be resolved, Berisha said: "Yes...They (the Socialist Party) could ask them to dissolve the committees...We are waiting."
Vlore was the focal point of protests which escalated into weeks of disorder after the collapse the savings schemes.
Southerners were among the hardest hit as thousands of people lost their life savings. Rebels have blamed Berisha, a northerner, and say they will not give up until he quits.
Vranitzky earlier appealed for "at least a minimum of dialogue" between the government and the rebels. But Berisha refused: "We are not negotiating with them. No," he said.

Vranitzky arrived in Tirana to criticisms in Rilindja Demokratike, the newspaper of Berisha's party. Another pro-Berisha daily, Albania, said his contacts with the rebels were a minefield that could blow up all hopes of peace.
Asked to comment, he said: "I have my duties and I have a mandate and I am definitely not going to let this mandate be curtailed by any newspaper reports."
Around a dozen youths protested outside Fino's office earlier with banners in Albanian and German reading "Vranitzky, be neutral" and "Don't meet the rebels". Police moved them on.
Vranitzky said after meeting Fino earlier in the day that the prime minister believed "having elections not later than June...is a must". He added: "I think they are right."
